Cause: The docindex application is configured with CLUSTER_SIZE=3 (visible in docindex-3's logs: "own ordinal 3 is outside the configured cluster (CLUSTER_SIZE=3); joining as standby"). While in standby, the pod intentionally returns HTTP 503 on /ready, so its readiness probe keeps failing ("Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503 (x290 over 48m)"). 

Because StatefulSets use OrderedReady pod management by default, the controller creates pods sequentially and will not create the next ordinal until the previous one is Running and Ready [cite: concepts/workloads/controllers/statefulset#deployment-and-scaling-guarantees-0] [cite: concepts/workloads/controllers/statefulset#pod-management-policies-0]. That is why docindex-3 is not taking traffic (not Ready) and docindex-4 was never created at all — the scale-up is blocked on docindex-3.

Fix (owner to apply): Update the docindex workload configuration so CLUSTER_SIZE reflects the new replica count (5), e.g. bump the CLUSTER_SIZE env var (or the ConfigMap it is sourced from) in the StatefulSet pod template from 3 to 5 and roll the pods. Once docindex-3 leaves standby and reports Ready, the StatefulSet controller will create docindex-4, which will also come up Ready and begin serving. No change to podManagementPolicy is needed; the issue is the app-level cluster membership, not the ordering guarantee.
